This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of [[:en:Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe, Wakayama]].
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of [[:en:Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe, Wakayama]].
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of [[:en:Tanabe, Wakayama|Tanabe, Wakayama]].
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.
== Sources == Key historical sources are abbreviated as follows:

'Guki' | [[:en:Fujiwara no Teika|Fujiwara no Teika]] | 1201 | Records of Kumano pilgrimage during Emperor Go-Toba’s reign. |}
== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.
== Sources == Key historical sources are abbreviated as follows:
{|class="wikitable" |+ Abbreviations of Historical Sources ! Abbreviation !! Author !! Year !! Notes |- ! 'Chūyūki' | {{ill|Fujiwara no Munetada|ja|藤原宗忠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara no Munetada|1=Fujiwara no Munetada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11623159}} | 1109 | 'Chūyūki' |- ! 'Guki' | {{ill|Fujiwara no Teika|en|Fujiwara no Teika|WD=Q378425|lt=Fujiwara no Teika}} | 1201 | Records of Kumano pilgrimage during Emperor Go-Toba’s reign. |}
== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Sanzan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi, Wakayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama|1=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549|1=Ōsakamoto Ōji Shrine}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi, Wakayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama|1=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549|1=Ōsakamoto Ōji Shrine}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi, Wakayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama|1=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549|1=Ōsakamoto Ōji Shrine}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi, Wakayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama|1=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549|1=Ōsakamoto Ōji Shrine}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi, Wakayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|WD=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama|1=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|WD=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|WD=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|WD=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|WD=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524549|1=Ōsakamoto Ōji Shrine}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>

This article discusses the '''{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}''' located within the former {{ill|Nakahechi, Wakayama|ja|中辺路町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi, Wakayama|1=Nakahechi, Wakayama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2327396}} area, now part of {{ill|Tanabe, Wakayama|en|Tanabe, Wakayama|qid=Q304266|lt=Tanabe, Wakayama|1=Tanabe, Wakayama}}.
== What are the Ninety-Nine Ōji? == {{Main|{{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}}}
The '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' refers to a group of shrines along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|en|Kumano Kodō|qid=Q17050475|lt=Kumano Kodō|1=Kumano Kodō}}, especially along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|1=Nakahechi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30074932}} routes. They were rapidly organized during the 12th to 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners to serve as spiritual waypoints for imperial and noble pilgrims on the {{ill|Kumano pilgrimage|ja|熊野詣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano pilgrimage|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野三山|1=Kumano Three Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10403700}}. Prayers for the protection of pilgrims were conducted at these shrines.
However, following the {{ill|Jōkyū War|en|Jōkyū War|qid=Q1372308|lt=Jōkyū War|1=Jōkyū War}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|1=Kyōto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q740246}} declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many Ōji along the Kiiji route. Despite efforts during the Edo period by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|qid=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}} to revitalize them, the shrines never fully regained their former prominence. The state-driven {{ill|State Shinto|en|State Shinto|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto|1=State Shinto}} policies of the Meiji era, shrine mergers, and urbanization further led to the loss or uncertainty of many shrine locations.
This article focuses on those Ninety-Nine Ōji whose locations are identified within Tanabe City, specifically the former Nakahechi area.
== Monuments and Milestones == [[Image:Stupa of OSAKAMOTO-oji remains.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Stone stupa near {{ill|Osakamoto Ōji|ja|大阪本王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osakamoto Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524549|1=Ōsakamoto Ōji Shrine}}]]
Along the Nakahechi route, between {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3514339}} and {{ill|Hongū Taisha|ja|本宮大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hongū Taisha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, distinct remnants can be observed:
One is the '''green schist monuments''' erected by the Kishū Domain in 1723 to commemorate the now-defunct Ōji sites.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 91]</ref> These can still be seen at places like Daimon, Hisohara, and Inohana.
Another is the '''stone stupas''' made of rhyolite, known as ''chōseki sotoba''.<ref>Kumanoji Editorial Committee [1973: 79]</ref> These served as distance markers, often engraved with Sanskrit characters, the distance from key points, and the names of donors.

== Ninety-Nine Ōji of Nakahechi, Tanabe City == There are 13 Ōji shrines within this area, including {{ill|Takijiri Ōji|ja|滝尻王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takijiri Ōji|1=Takijiri Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3514339}}, {{ill|Daimon Ōji|ja|大門王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daimon Ōji|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 九十九王子 (田辺市中辺路町)|1=List of Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines (Tanabe City, Nakahechi Town)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11370053}}, {{ill|Chikatsuyu Ōji|ja|近露王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikatsuyu Ōji|1=Chikatsuyu Ōji Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11639127}}, and others, designated as part of the {{ill|Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja|熊野参詣道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Pilgrimage Route|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17050475}}, a National Historic Site.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=https://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_kinenbutsu.html|title=Designated Cultural Properties of Tanabe City - Monuments|publisher=Tanabe City Board of Education|accessdate=2009-03-20}}</ref>
